name: Chess training
title: Chess training | Daily puzzles, tactics and game analysis
description: Improve your chess with daily puzzles, tactics and calculation practice. Study real games, analyze positions and build a weekly training habit.

/.title: Chess training | Daily puzzles, tactics and game analysis
/.description: Improve your chess with daily puzzles, tactics and calculation practice. Study real games, analyze positions and build a weekly training habit.

/practice.title: Chess practice modes
/practice.description: Pick a chess training mode: daily puzzle and review, mates and tactics, calculation, threats and sacrifices, position judgment, openings and endgames. Every position comes from a real game.

/practice/daily.title: Daily chess puzzle
/practice/daily.description: Solve a new chess puzzle every day, the same for everyone. Each one comes from a real game and asks you to find every good move in the position.

/practice/good-moves.title: Good moves: chess candidate move puzzles
/practice/good-moves.description: Chess positions with several good moves: find them all before you commit. Puzzles from real games that train candidate move thinking.

/practice/mate-in-one.title: Mate in 1 chess puzzles
/practice/mate-in-one.description: Find the mating move in positions from real games. One try per puzzle, with a rating that follows your results as you practice.

/practice/mate-in-three.title: Mate in 3 chess puzzles
/practice/mate-in-three.description: Play the mating line move by move in positions from real games. One try per puzzle, with a rating that follows your results as you practice.

/practice/tactics.title: Chess tactics practice
/practice/tactics.description: Test your tactics with puzzles from real games: find the best move or play the winning line. One try each, and your rating follows your results.

/practice/look-ahead.title: Look ahead: chess calculation practice
/practice/look-ahead.description: Practice calculating three moves ahead. Find every good line in real chess positions and meet your opponent’s best replies before you make your move.

/practice/review.title: Chess puzzle review
/practice/review.description: Missed chess puzzles come back after 1, 3 and 7 days, from every practice mode, plus the mistakes the engine finds in your own saved games.

/practice/threats.title: What’s the threat? Chess practice
/practice/threats.description: Spot what your opponent threatens in positions from real games, then find a move that stops it. Train the first question of every chess move.

/practice/who-is-better.title: Who is better? Chess evaluation practice
/practice/who-is-better.description: Judge quiet positions from real games: White better, equal or Black better. Then see the engine’s score and the main imbalance on the board.

/practice/spot-the-feature.title: Spot the feature: pawn structure practice
/practice/spot-the-feature.description: Tap the isolated, doubled, backward and passed pawns, the outposts and the open files in positions from real chess games.

/practice/is-it-safe.title: Is it safe? Chess blunder-check practice
/practice/is-it-safe.description: A tempting capture or check from a real game: play it or not? If it fails, show the refutation. Train the blunder check before every move.

/practice/see-it.title: See it in your head: chess visualization
/practice/see-it.description: Read a few moves while the board stays still, then answer where the pieces stand. Chess visualization practice built from real games.

/practice/opening-moves.title: Chess opening principles practice
/practice/opening-moves.description: Positions from moves 4 to 12 of real games where a player went wrong: find the move that follows the opening principles, or spot the mistake.

/practice/sound-sacrifice.title: Sound sacrifice? Chess practice
/practice/sound-sacrifice.description: Sacrifices from real games, checked by the engine: judge whether each one is sound, unsound or unclear, then play the critical reply.

/practice/chess-basics.title: Chess basics quiz: moves, values and notation
/practice/chess-basics.description: Multiple-choice questions for beginners: how each chess piece moves, what it is worth, and how moves are written, including Rad1, Nbd2 and R1a3.

/practice/endgames.title: Chess endgame technique practice
/practice/endgames.description: Endgame puzzles from real games by type: pawn, rook, minor piece and queen endings, plus the stalemate traps in won positions.

/theory.title: Chess theory lessons
/theory.description: 26 short chess lessons on how strong players think: openings, pawn structures, calculation, strategy, endgames and psychology, with practice on real positions.

/theory/chess-basics.title: Chess basics: how pieces move, piece values and notation
/theory/chess-basics.description: A beginner’s chess lesson: how each piece moves, castling, en passant and promotion, what the pieces are worth, and how to write a game down in algebraic notation.

/theory/opening-principles.title: Chess opening principles
/theory/opening-principles.description: How to start a chess game well: control the center, develop your pieces, keep your king safe and know why each opening move is played.

/theory/pawn-structures.title: Chess pawn structures explained
/theory/pawn-structures.description: Isolated, doubled, backward and passed pawns and pawn chains: how the pawn structure points to the right plan in a chess game.

/theory/ccto.title: CCTO: a method for finding chess moves
/theory/ccto.description: Checks, captures, threats, optimization: a simple order for finding chess moves, with examples, common mistakes and five exercises.

/theory/decision-making.title: Making decisions in a chess game
/theory/decision-making.description: Spot the critical moments, choose what to calculate and manage your clock: a practical decision routine for every chess game you play.

/theory/chess-psychology.title: Chess psychology and focus
/theory/chess-psychology.description: Play the position, not the rating: how to stay focused, recover after a mistake and keep a clear head in your chess games and tournaments.

/theory/analyzing-your-games.title: How to analyze your own chess games
/theory/analyzing-your-games.description: Analyze your chess games before the engine, sort your mistakes by type and turn them into a personal training plan with a simple game journal.

/theory/candidate-moves.title: Candidate moves in chess
/theory/candidate-moves.description: Before you calculate, list the two to four moves worth checking. Candidate moves and the tree of analysis, inspired by Alexander Kotov, with an example.

/theory/explain-every-move.title: Explain every chess move
/theory/explain-every-move.description: A move teaches you something only when you can say why it was played. Learn to name the problem each move solves. Inspired by John Nunn.

/theory/step-by-step-training.title: Learn chess tactics in small steps
/theory/step-by-step-training.description: Master one tactical motif at a time: recognize it, apply it, then combine it with another. Inspired by Rob Brunia and Cor van Wijgerden.

/theory/structured-improvement.title: Study chess, then check yourself
/theory/structured-improvement.description: A training loop that works: one topic, one example, five puzzles without hints, then a review of every mistake. Inspired by Artur Yusupov.

/theory/position-imbalances.title: Chess imbalances and planning
/theory/position-imbalances.description: Not every advantage is counted in pawns. Compare activity, pawn structure, open files and weak squares to find your plan. Inspired by Jeremy Silman.

/theory/prophylaxis.title: Prophylaxis in chess
/theory/prophylaxis.description: Ask what your opponent wants, then take it away. Prophylactic thinking and active defense in chess, inspired by Tigran Petrosian.

/theory/blockade-and-outposts.title: Blockades and outposts in chess
/theory/blockade-and-outposts.description: Stop a weak pawn with a strong piece in front of it and give your knights secure outposts. Positional play inspired by Aron Nimzowitsch.

/theory/clear-endgame-thinking.title: Simplify to win chess endgames
/theory/clear-endgame-thinking.description: When you are ahead, the right trades make winning easier. Learn which exchanges help and which lead to a draw. Inspired by José Raúl Capablanca.

/theory/practical-endgames.title: Chess endgame strategy: plan first
/theory/practical-endgames.description: In the endgame there is often no hurry: improve your king and pieces, create a second weakness, then strike. Inspired by Mikhail Shereshevsky.

/theory/calculate-critical-lines.title: Calculate the critical line in chess
/theory/calculate-critical-lines.description: Find the moment when one exact move decides the game, then calculate it to a clear position against the best defense. Inspired by Mark Dvoretsky.

/theory/initiative-and-sacrifice.title: Initiative and sacrifice in chess
/theory/initiative-and-sacrifice.description: A beautiful sacrifice is not always a correct one. Name what you give up, what you get back and how the opponent defends. Inspired by Mikhail Tal.

/theory/board-visualization.title: Chess visualization training
/theory/board-visualization.description: Hold the position in your head: short memorize, hide and check exercises that build the board vision you need to calculate. Inspired by János Flesch.

/theory/practical-improvement.title: Practical chess improvement
/theory/practical-improvement.description: Why many players stop improving, and a five-step training loop that turns your own mistakes into targeted practice. Inspired by IM Yevhenii Yelisieiev.

/theory/strategic-plans.title: How to find a strategic plan in chess
/theory/strategic-plans.description: When no tactic is in sight, read the weak squares, piece activity, pawn breaks and trades, then pick a plan with a concrete first move.

/theory/positions-without-hints.title: Find the best chess move without a hint
/theory/positions-without-hints.description: Real games have no puzzle titles. Learn to tell whether a position needs attack, defense, a positional move or technique before you look for the move.

/theory/sacrifice-compensation.title: When is a chess sacrifice justified?
/theory/sacrifice-compensation.description: Tactical, positional and speculative sacrifices: how to check that your compensation survives the best defense. Inspired by Andrei Volokitin.

/theory/piece-maneuvering.title: The art of maneuvering in chess
/theory/piece-maneuvering.description: Improve your worst piece with a real route: knight transfers, open diagonals, open files and a second weakness. Inspired by Adrian Mikhalchishin.

/theory/calculation-discipline.title: Disciplined calculation in chess
/theory/calculation-discipline.description: Choose candidates first, keep the board in your head accurate, check the strongest defense and judge the final position. Inspired by Mykhaylo Oleksiyenko.

/theory/stop-repeating-mistakes.title: How to stop repeating chess mistakes
/theory/stop-repeating-mistakes.description: A five-step pre-move check, the usual causes of blunders and a simple loop to stop making the same chess mistakes. Inspired by Igor Smirnov.

/library.title: Chess library
/library.description: Replay real chess games, analyze any position with Stockfish and keep your saved games in one place: everything you need to study chess.

/library/board.title: Chess analysis board
/library/board.description: Analyze chess positions and games with Stockfish. Set up a board or paste a PGN, pick your candidate moves and compare them with the engine.

/library/games.title: Chess games to study and solve
/library/games.description: Browse real chess games by theme, level, opening and training focus. Replay each game, study its ideas and solve the key positions along the way.

/library/games/:id.title: Chess game replay and training
/library/games/:id.description: Replay a real chess game move by move. Explore its critical positions, compare candidate moves and practice finding the best continuation.

/library/saved.title: My saved chess games
/library/saved.description: Return to your saved chess games and positions. Review your analysis and continue studying in your personal Chess training library.

/privacy.title: Privacy policy
/privacy.description: What Chess training stores, why it stores it, which services it uses and how to delete your account and all of your data.

/support.title: Support
/support.description: Get help with Chess training: contact us, report a bug, restore your progress or delete your account and data.

/licenses.title: Licenses and credits
/licenses.description: Chess training is free software under the GPL-3.0. See its source code and the projects it builds on, such as Stockfish and Chessground.

/sign-in.title: Sign in
/sign-in.description: Sign in to Chess training with your Google account to save games and keep track of your chess practice.

/profile.title: Your chess training profile
/profile.description: View your Chess training profile, review your practice progress and manage your account preferences.
